newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle prices seen steady - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle prices seen steady - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle next week were expected to trade in light volume at steady prices amid thin holiday-dominated demand, feedlot sources said.
Packers reportedly had adequate inventory for next week's holiday-shortened schedules. Meat packers will be closed Wednesday in observance of Christmas.
Sales Friday were light at $65.00 to $65.25 per cwt, steady to $0.25 higher compared with the bulk of this week's activity, according to private sources and USDA.
About 4,800 sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area and 1,500 in Kansas, USDA said. Most showlists were sold.
Friday's USDA monthly Cattle-on-Feed Report was not seen having an impact on fed cattle prices next week because there were no major surprises in the report, some cattle feeders said.

The seven state portion of the report showed an increase of three percent on feed as of December 1, compared with a year earlier. Placements during November were eight percent more than a year ago and November marketings ran three percent below November of 1995.
